utterances.text: I'm speaking about your personal observation, and I'm just asking a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally I didn't see the bomb land, but I heard it after which I saw Katolicka Street on fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What you told us earlier that you had heard was an explosion, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And from the hill you saw fire?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And that's the extent of your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have personal knowledge from my subordinate officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm just asking of your knowledge. You've explained about your subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. It is as you say.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, when this statement was made, this is in December 2002, the trial against Slobodan Milosevic was underway in The Hague, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I do remember, though, that I testified here in 2005. I really cannot recall when his trial began.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall when he was arrested, Mr. Milosevic? I mean, that must have been in the news in your country, no? Covered quite extensively?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It was widely covered. Everyone was talking about it in our country.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in March or April, perhaps late March, early April of 2000 or 2001. I'm not sure. No, not 2000, 2001 probably.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And are you aware, sir, that the indictment against Mr. Milosevic included allegations regarding the destruction of the old town of Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the indictment against Mr. Milosevic, there are all sorts of allegations from the original sin onwards. Among others, allegations about Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So I take that as a yes. Sir, are you aware that this commission for -- or the so-called Commission for the Co-operation with the ICTY was established by General Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who established it. In any case, I followed their order or request.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you recall approximately when it was established?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it must have been at some time before they summoned me. I really don't know when it was established exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And in this statement you say - this is at the end - you say: "I declare that my unit and I did not have anything to do with the allege destruction either of this part of Djakovica town or of this place of worship." Do you recall saying that, sir, in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, I can see it before me. That's what I said. I still stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you came here to testify in the defence of Mr. Milosevic, you brought this statement with you, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I brought it with me or if I handed it over to an attorney in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this was one of the statements that you made to the commission that was discussed during your testimony in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to look at another of these statements, sir. This is D689.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this is a statement dated the previous day, 27th December, 2002. And it refers to unit activities on 1st April, 1999. Do you recall going over this one yesterday with my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And can I take it, sir, that this statement was prepared in the same way as the previous one we've looked at?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you were again called by members of the commission and shown portions of the report "As Seen, As Told" that concerned events in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And on the basis of what you read, then you prepared this statement that we have here?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Based on what I could remember and what I read, that is how I drew up the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, I have a question in relation to this statement. You say - and this is towards --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Maybe we can see page 2 on the screen in both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You say in the almost two last paragraphs: "I learned of the alleged crime committed in the Cerim quarter from the Humanitarian Law Fund book, "Kosovo: As Seen" -- here it's written, "As written or As Told." And then you say: "I affirm that no one from my unit has any connection with the alleged crime in the Cerim quarter." Having read this statement of yours, sir, I'm just wondering which alleged crime in the Cerim quarter you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "alleged." I believe in Serbian it said the "aforementioned," which is different. Allegedly, that is something that one claims. Although, it may be uncertain. It could be hypothetical. That's what allegedly means in our language.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. But, sir, which crime are you referring to in the Cerim district that you are denying having had any connection with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this alleged crime that is written about in this book of the Humanitarian Law Fund. In this statement, I'm actually responding to some of the paragraphs in that book where this alleged crime in Cerim is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And which crime is that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It mentions some civilians there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what specifically did it say about these civilians, this book? I'm just trying to understand what your statement is about because it's not explained there.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A picture was shown there. I think it was a house, a burned-down house. And it said something about a street. I don't even know where that street is, but an alleged crime was described there. I read that and then I wrote on the basis of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what had had happened at this house according to the report?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I can't remember exactly, but I know that what was mentioned was an alleged crime against some civilians as far as I can remember. Now, it's been quite awhile, but as far as I can remember, that is what it was about. And also about the burning of some house.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This alleged crime against civilians, would that have been a massacre, sir, in the Cerim district?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I say alleged crime, then I could say alleged massacre as well, you see. You are saying alleged crime to me now and then you you give me a concrete form of crime. I don't know how to define it now, but what I said here was that as for this alleged crime that was described in the book, I have no knowledge about it whatsoever. But I claim that it certainly wasn't committed by any member of my unit, that alleged crime, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So you are denying any participation in an alleged crime, but you don't remember which crime that was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, in this statement you refer - and this is on the same page we are looking at - to a statement by a 3rd Battalion commander, Major Dusko Vukasinovic. Do you see that? You say: "According to a statement, one of the platoons was located in Vinarski Podrum facility in the immediate vicinity of the Cerim quarter."

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Is this a statement you looked at before preparing your own statement about this alleged crime in the Cerim district?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When the commission called me and when they gave me the task to describe that event, I then called the commander of the unit that was nearby, that was a wine cellar, Vinarski Podrum, and I asked him whether he had any knowledge of that alleged crime. I told him to write up what he had said to me then. As I read his statement, I then wrote my own statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this wine cellar that you referred to, Vinarski Podrum, is that a locality where members of your brigade were based?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Part of the unit, a smaller unit, perhaps a platoon. Maximum up to 20 men, perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And was this also in the Cerim district?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you know which neighbourhood of Djakovica that was?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's on the right-hand side of the road. Perhaps it's 400 or 500 metres away from the Cerim neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in your statement you say that on the night of the 1st of April, you travelled by -- you headed to Djakovica town to the bridge command post and you travelled this route and once again observed no activities in the Cerim quarter?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you just happen to have been driving through the Cerim quarter on the night of the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't just happen. That night, or rather, the 30th of April [as interpreted], we had a unit of ours in Ljug Bunar which is also not very far away from Cerim and radar of ours was hit there and two of my soldiers got killed on that occasion. We were then trying to get them out to rescue them, and when that job, I mean, maybe I shouldn't say job, activity, when that was over, then I left and went to the command post, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, are you aware that the -- oh, I'm sorry, I see my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Just for the transcript, the date that was registered in the previous answer, could my colleague just have a look at that and could she perhaps check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz, I leave that to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I was speaking about the night of the 1st of April, and we have on the transcript that you are referring to that night the 30th of April. Is that correct? That you were speaking about the 30th of April?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have a look at my statement? If that's what the statement says. No, that our radar was hit on the 31st, between the 31st and the 1st. Around 2300 hours on the 31st. As we are extinguishing the fire, as we were trying to save the soldiers, it did actually spill over to the 1st, so I was going back on the 1st of April, yes, it would be the 1st of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So you are speaking about the night from the 31st to the 1st of April? 31st of March to the 1st of April?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you say in your statement that you have no information of any kind about an alleged crime in this quarter, in the Cerim quarter?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Are you aware, sir, that the indictment against Mr. Milosevic contains specific allegations concerning the Cerim quarter? When I'm speaking about specific allegations, I mean a massacre of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what I'm supposed to answer in relation to that. Do I know that that is written in the indictment? As I have already said, everything is written in the indictment against Mr. Milosevic. If you are asking me about a specific event, I hereby state that I have no knowledge about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking specifically if you knew that Mr. Milosevic when he was on trial here at The Hague was accused, among other things, of a massacre in the Cerim quarter, massacre of civilians, specifically on Milos Gilic Street?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that that question was put when I was testifying here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are aware that that was one of the allegations against him at the time when this statement was prepared?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I testified here, I knew that that question was being asked because he asked me about that too. When I wrote this statement, I did not know that that was contained in his indictment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you had read specific allegations in the report, "As Seen, As Told," about events in that district, before preparing your statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. On the basis of that which was written in that book of the Humanitarian Law Fund, I was actually given the task of writing my statement, otherwise, I wouldn't have known about that, about that event. And I never would have thought about that. I mean, when I received that book, then I read what was written there about Cerim.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we've had testimony here from former residents of the Cerim district about a massacre that took place on 157 Milos Gilic Street, and it's a massacre that involved the killing of 20 civilians in a house which was later burnt down. Have you heard about that incident, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read that in that book otherwise, I hadn't heard of it. How else would I have heard about it? I did not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you do recall what the specific allegations or the alleged crime referred to in your report had to do with?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Some civilians were being referred to in a house, but I couldn't remember the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, based on the evidence we have of persons who were in the neighbourhood at the time these civilians were shot at by members of the MUP, killed, and then the house was set on fire, did you know about that incident, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Had a massacre of that nature taken place in the Cerim district, would that have been reported to you by members of your unit who were on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Had they had such knowledge, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And had a massacre of that nature taken place, would that also have been reported to the head of the SUP in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had found out about something like that, I would have notified him about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In fact, sir, if a massacre of that nature had taken place in the Cerim district, it would have been quite difficult to hide it, no? It would have been -- information about that would have been shared and would have become known by you and by the head of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I had not found out about that. I cannot make any assumptions. I didn't find out about anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir. I want to move away from this statement now and ask you about some testimony you gave yesterday regarding the large-scale movement of the civilian population in Kosovo. Do you remember speaking being that, sir, yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. There were movements by civilians. Now, the question was what people considered to be large scale. I said that I saw groups of people. The biggest group that I had seen was between 200 and 300 persons. There was movement, yes, and now what people say in terms of what was large scale or smaller scale, that varies, but there were -- there was movement by people, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said, sir, yesterday, that when the NATO bombing began in March of 1999, you began seeing this movement on a daily basis, and I believe you gave the same numbers you've just given, 200, 300 persons? Do you recall giving that testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if not every day, but it was frequent at any rate. Very frequent. Since I was not in Djakovica every day but when I was there, there was movement very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, you said that some five or six or ten days after the NATO bombing began, especially when people started talking about ammunition with depleted uranium, and you said - and these are your words - "they arrived in waves." You were speaking about the refugees. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't ammunition that was coming in waves, it was refugees that were coming in waves, yes, that is what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said they weren't single families, they were, in fact, large groups moved on foot and tractors?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were certain places where they would gather and wait for one another, and then they would continue their journey together.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you say they would continue their journey together, I understand from the evidence you gave yesterday that they were continuing a journey leaving Djakovica, in fact? They were heading out of Djakovica town?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the the most part, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this reference you made to "they arrived in waves," this would mean that, if I understand you correctly, approximately towards the beginning of April, that is six or ten days after the NATO bombing campaign began, end of March, beginning of April, that is when you saw the largest groups of refugees heading out of town, these waves of refugees that you are speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the most part, the beginning of April or end of March.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So that was the period when you saw the largest groups of refugees heading out of town? End of March, beginning of April?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, yesterday and also today you said that -- you you referred to the fact that these persons were leaving for fear of ammunition containing depleted uranium. In fact, yesterday you said that these waves of refugees, you started seeing them after people started talking about ammunition with depleted uranium; do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall saying that, but I did not say that that was the main reason. I said one of the reasons. I said there was the bombing, any kind of bombing, then at the end I said knowledge that depleted uranium ammunition was being used.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you have also today indicated other causes not only depleted uranium, but you did say that this was one of the causes that you considered to be the reason why these persons were leaving, fear of ammunition being used by NATO containing depleted uranium?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, inter alia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And how do you know that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that because certain people talked to refugees and there was -- there was talk going around town that depleted uranium ammunition made men sterile, and that is what they were particularly afraid of. That was their concern about their offspring. That's what I heard from some of my soldiers and officers. I had soldiers and officers from Djakovica who knew people who were leaving. They had talked to them. I didn't hear that from anyone because I didn't talk to anyone since I don't speak a word of Albanian, but I did hear these things. I had knowledge of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, so this is not personal knowledge? You spoke to no one about this? You did not ask the refugees yourself about this?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not talk to a single refugee who had said that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, earlier in this case, some weeks ago, we had the testimony of General Petkovic, the chief of administration of land forces. Do you know who he is?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And General Petkovic told us that he conducted some sort of study on the use of depleted uranium by NATO, and he said that the first physical samples of this type of ammunition being used in Kosovo was not found until sometime in late April, sometime around 20th of April, 1999. Do you accept that testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I can give a reference. I believe this is in his statement D512, page 2. The date of 18th of April is given.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, this would have been -- 18th of April would have been well after the time when you said you saw the large waves of refugees leaving town, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot fully agree with him because I was in Djakovica, and I saw an A-10 aircraft operating. That is the only aircraft that uses depleted uranium ammunition in addition to cruise missiles that can also have warheads containing depleted uranium. However, now you are trying to say to me that the use of depleted uranium ammunition was the only reason for population movement, but I said --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, sir, sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that was one of the reasons.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not suggesting that. I'm just referring you to your statement of yesterday when you said that the refugees began arriving in waves when word spread that NATO was using depleted uranium. And you have told us that you recall saying that yesterday, so I'm not suggesting that that is the only reason that you said was the cause of the movement. But you, in fact, had no personal knowledge that that was the reason why the refugees were leaving in such large waves towards the end of March, early April?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that that was one of the reasons, that they had heard --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not challenging that you said there were other reasons. What I'm asking you specifically is, or what I'm putting to you is that you had no personal knowledge that that was the reason why there was such a large-scale movement, these waves of refugees leaving Djakovica town in the end of March, early April? You have no personal knowledge that this was one of the reasons?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You are, in fact, sir, just simply speculating that that was the reason that they were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm not speculating. I don't speak Albanian. I didn't discuss this with any of the refugees, but I had information coming from my officers and soldiers who could speak Albanian who told me that. Personally, I didn't speak to a single refugee.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I was just asking for your personal knowledge, sir. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think it's time for the break. I think Your Honour indicated that we are breaking at 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, we will break now and resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I want to now turn your attention to an operation that you spoke about extensively during your testimony, and this is an operation with a code-name Reka. Do you remember being asked some questions about that by my learned colleague?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was actually an action called Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. We'll refer to it as action Reka. I understood from your testimony, sir, that this is an action that took place over two days, the 27th and 28th of April, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've indicated that a logistic battalion of your brigade under the command of Zlatko Odak took part in this operation? I apologise if the pronunciation of the name is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your pronunciation was quite good, however, the name of the unit is incorrect. It was not a battalion. It was a company. The difference is quite important in terms of size. Major Odak was the commander of the logistics battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I think I misspoke there. So it's a company from this logistic battalion which was commanded by Major Zlatko Odak, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I think you spoke about this action taking place in the Carragojs valley?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I pronounce it as Carragojs, that's how it's spelled, and that's how I pronounce it, although I'm not positive that is the correct name. In any case, we refer to that area as Reka.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the general area of Reka, does that also include the Trava valley?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So I said general, we won't be too picky with pronunciations here, so don't worry about that. The village of Meja, sir, is this a village that is close to the town of Djakovica, in fact, just outside the town?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's some 7 or 8 kilometres away from the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And would it be correct to say that this village, if you are heading out of Djakovica going west, this would be somewhere towards the start of this Carragojs valley area?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so. I suppose so. I have never been to Meja and I don't really know that exactly. Although, I suppose it is in that general area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And you've told us, sir, during the course of your evidence, that this company from your brigade was deployed on Cabrat hill? You've, in fact, marked it on a map; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you said that the highest point of this hill was of above Djakovica town?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, in fact, the area where your company was deployed was a vantage point in that area, from where you would have visibility to localities surrounding Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not. From that place one could not observe Djakovica. You could only observe the rear where the company was deployed. It was at an elevation. They could see this way, but on the other side there is a forest, and it is still pretty far from Djakovica. That is not the place at Cabrat hill where I was when the aggression started. It's not the same place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Maybe my question wasn't clear. I wasn't saying whether it was vantage point to look out to Djakovica, but you were high enough so you could look in the point opposite direction? So looking west?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: From that place, well, to the west, it's actually south-west, but one can't see much from there. It is at the edge of a forest. I visited them, and I saw their positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've told us that this action, Reka, was led by Milan Kotur from the Pristina Corps forward command post?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By decision of the forward command post of the Pristina Corps, he commanded that action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You also said that the purpose of the action was to neutralise terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the basic goal of that action was to have that area, which is strategically very important, in which there was a great number of terrorists, and from which they made incursions and carried out attacks on our columns to neutralise that area, to have the area clear of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You also said, sir -- well, before I put that question, on the days preceding the Reka action there had been a killing by the KLA of five policemen in the general area of Meja; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard something about that, but well, yes, I think it happened. As for whether five people were killed or if there was anyone wounded, that's something I'm not completely sure of.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: A local policeman by the name of Milutin Prascevic was among those killed, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think his name was Prascevic or Prosevic, in any case, similar to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And this was someone you knew yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you testified about this action in the Milosevic case, and this is at page 45436 of the transcript, you were asked about this action. And you said: "It was common knowledge that that part belongs to the general area of Reka and there were many terrorists." And then you say: "It was an area where terrorists engaged in large-scale operations and activities, and it's true that terrorists killed five policemen." And you were referring to a statement that was being put to you and you said: "He mentions Prascevic, I knew Prascevic myself." Is that correct, sir, the evidence that you gave in the Milosevic case, that Prascevic was a policeman that you knew yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of him, but I didn't know him personally. Prascevic, I couldn't recognise that person if I met him.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you don't recall saying when you testified here earlier that this was, in fact, a person that you knew yourself?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, in relation to this same action, you say: "As for Meja" - and this, I'm reading your Milosevic transcript, same page - "it was an anti-terrorist operation exclusively which was legal, lawful with the aim of rounding up the killers of those policemen." Do you stand by that statement, sir, that this was a legal, lawful action aimed at rounding up the killers of these five policemen?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was not the goal of that action, and it wasn't the only goal. Quite a contrary. I think the basic goal of the action was to neutralise the Siptar terrorist forces in that area --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as to secure --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I just want to go back to my question. I read something out to you, and I'm just asking if you stand by what you said in the Milosevic case? I can read it out again, that this was a legal, lawful --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That this was a legal, lawful action with the aim of rounding up the killers of these policemen. This is what you said when you testified here the previous time. Do you stand by that, sir? It's really just a yes or no question.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to tell you whether I said so or -- could you please repeat. I'm not sure what I should answer to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm putting to you what you said when you testified here previously as to the aim of this action, and I'm asking whether you stand by that statement, by what you said when you testified in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't sufficiently explain the basic goal of that action when I said that. Perhaps I didn't use the right words to explain what was the main reason for that action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not sure you are answering my question, sir. I understand that you are saying there might be more than one goal for the action, I'm just asking if this was one of the aims, to round up the killers of the five policemen, which is what you said when you testified here the previous time?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to know the question put to me at the time. Was the question for me to enumerate all the goals of that action or maybe the question was put in such a way that I provided this answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, the question simply -- you were being put a statement by another witness and this is a statement you gave on your own about the action, and all I'm asking, sir, is whether you stand by it or not, and I don't believe you are answering my question. It's simply just a yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that the basic goal of the action Reka was to neutralise the Siptar terrorist forces in the Carragojs valley. As for whether it was legal, of course it was. It was a legal action. It had been planned and of course, among other things, one of the goals was to catch the killers of those policemen. This was one of many incidents which took place.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And that was all I was asking, sir. Now, if we move on from this point, this action, the Reka action, did not only involve a company from your brigade. In fact, it involved many units from other brigades as well, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several units participated, among others mine.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And among those units that participated was the 125th Motorised Brigade, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that one. It is possible that it participated.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you don't recall hearing about that from Major Odak, which units were involved?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Odak could only have seen the units which were adjacent to him. This was the second battalion of the 549th Brigade. He could not have known of the participation of other units. The 125th Brigade was at Kosare, in that part of the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've referred to the 2nd Battalion of the 549th Brigade, do you know who commanded that battalion?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of that battalion was Colonel Vlatko Vukovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you say you don't have any recollection of whether the 125th Motorised Brigade participated in this action; am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it participated or not. It may have, it may have not. It was decided by the person who planned the action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to show you a document in connection to this action.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is P950. If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is a document dated 27th of April, 1999, sent by the 125th Motorised Brigade Command to the Pristina Corps Command in the Djakovica forward command. You have the document there, sir, in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it. I can see it as a document of the 125th Motorised Brigade although it's a bit difficult to read. In any case, I can see it's their document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2, and I'm looking for number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm just waiting for that to be up on your screen, sir. We see that the second sentence of number 2 says: "Part of the forces is engaged in mopping up the terrain from STS in the general area of Reka in keeping with your decision." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which item was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Units of the brigade are focused on reinforcement, setting up obstacles." I don't see that. On page 1 or page 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Second sentence of number 2.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Part of the forces is engaged in mopping up the terrain from STS in the general area of Reka, in keeping with your decision." Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I know this is not a document from your brigade, sir, but would you agree with me based on what we've been discussing that this reference here to the general area of Reka is, in fact, a reference to the same action that we've been speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we see in the Serbian version - it's not up on the screen in the English - that this is a document that was sent by the commander Colonel Dragan Zivanovic. That would be the commander of the 125th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In addition to this unit that we spoke about, the battalion from the 549th and the 125th Brigade and the elements from your brigade that you spoke about, do you know, sir, that there were also -- or there was also a MUP unit involved in this action? Do you have any information on that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only have information about my unit and the unit adjacent to mine. As for the rest of the forces, including the 125th Brigade, I have no information or knowledge about that. They may have been there and yet they may not have. I have no knowledge based on which I could assert that they did or did not participate.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. And if we could just have another document up since you've mentioned the 125th. This is P920.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, I was speaking specifically about whether there was a MUP unit involved, and you responded as for the rest of the forces including the 125th Brigade you have no information of knowledge. I'm understanding that also includes the MUP unit, you had no information of whether there was a MUP unit involved?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we look at the document here in front of you, sir, we see it is again a document from the command of the 125th Motorised Brigade. This is dated 28th April. So it's the day following the document that we just looked at. And we see that this is a regular combat report sent by this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And I would like to go in this document, I believe it's on the same page in the B/C/S, but in the English it's number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the second sentence says: "Some forces have been used to clear the terrain of STS in the general Reka sector, as per your decision." Again, sir, based on what we've been discussing here, would you agree with me that this reference here to an action or participation in clearing the terrain in the general Reka sector will be -- is a reference to the same Reka action that we've been speaking about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, sir, we'll move away from this document and while you were being questioned about this action by my learned colleague, you were shown a statement that you gave to the Commission for Co-operation with the ICTY, and this is D703.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is a statement dated 27th December, 2002. Do you recall discussing this with my learned colleague during your testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And, sir, if I understood your testimony yesterday correctly, you wrote this after you read allegations in what you've referred to as a book called "As Seen, As Told?"

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we've already looked at two other statements of yours that were given to this commission. I understand, sir, from your evidence that this statement that we have here, the 27th of December, 2002 statement was prepared in a similar fashion as the other ones that you've prepared, that is, you were called by the commission, shown these allegations, and asked to respond to them?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, if we turn to page 2 of this statement, and I just want to direct your attention to the second paragraph. It's a paragraph starting with: "On 27th and 28th of April, part of my unit, the intervention company, which comprised sections of the logistics battalion and command battalion, participated in an operation to seal off the designated territory in the Cabrat sector from elevation 478 to k. 442 (overlooking the poultry farm)" it says. Is this the same positions you were referring to yesterday during the course of your evidence when you drew on the map the location of your unit on Cabrat hill?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not quite understand the interpretation I received. So could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: It was a rather long question so probably my fault, sir. I just read a passage which is the second paragraph here, and my question was just simple. It refers to your -- part of your unit being deployed on Cabrat hill. Yesterday you drew on a map an area of deployment, and I'm just asking you to confirm whether what you drew on the map yesterday refers to the same area that's being discussed in the statement that you prepared?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. What I drew yesterday does relate to the positions of my unit on Cabrat hill, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, earlier today, sir, my colleague was putting to you several - I think it was at the beginning of today's session - several passages of the statement of one of your subordinates, Nike Peraj. Do you recall going through several passages of that with my learned colleague earlier today?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recall that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And there was one passage, in, I believe, it was paragraph 65 of Nike Peraj's statement which referred to this operation Reka being commanded from the forward command post by several officers including General Lazarevic. Do you remember that was put to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that that is what was written in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you told us, sir, that that was not true? You said it was, I believe the words you used was "physically impossible." This is at transcript page 2, line 14 onwards of today's transcript. Because you said that General Lazarevic was, in fact, with you on the 27th of April in Pristina. Do you recall that, sir, saying that it was physical impossible --

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 27th of April, not the 28th. He was with me on the 27th of April, not the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I said 27th of April, sir. And the passage, in fact, in Mr. Peraj's statement referred to the 27th, and you said that is not true, General Lazarevic was with me. Do you recall saying that, it was physically impossible because he was in Pristina with you attending, I think, an award ceremony, did you say, sir? That you were attending an award ceremony on the 27th of April in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were together at that ceremony.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, just drawing your attention to paragraph 3 of this statement that you yourself wrote, you say: "Between 1300 hours and 1400 hours on the 27th of April, 1999, I personally inspected the unit on the sealed-off line and ensured that they had taken correct position." And you say: "As I did so, I pointed out some minor things they had failed to do while fortifying the camouflage position because NATO aircraft were flying over the area the whole time." Do you see that paragraph, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, sir, it is in fact physically impossible, using your same words, for you to be at an award ceremony with General Lazarevic in Pristina and also be inspecting the line -- the sealed-off line that your unit had set up on Cabrat hill, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. I reviewed the unit perhaps somewhat later. I inspected it somewhat later. When I wrote this statement I really could not remember all details. This statement was written on the basis of memory only, without any documents. I'm not sure, I mean, I wrote that it was between 13- and 1400 hours, but it must have been somewhat later. I arrived from Pristina via Igarevo and Kijevo which is the shortest route. Now that I go back, as I try to remember it, it was on the same day but it must have been later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are saying that General Lazarevic was with you part of that day but not the whole day because you did spend part of the day reviewing your -- or inspecting your units up on Cabrat hill?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there, or rather, I left the ceremony before he did. I don't know how long he stayed there, but I came straight there to inspect that unit after the ceremony. In a way, it was in passing that I did that because that is the way you do go to Djakovica anyway.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you say you have no idea how long General Lazarevic remained at the ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You, in fact, have no idea of what were the whereabouts of General Lazarevic for the rest of that day because he wasn't with you clearly?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. It's not for me to ask General Lazarevic where he is, but I did leave and he stayed on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So when you said, sir, that the statement made by Mr. Peraj that General Lazarevic was commanding the action from the forward command post, Djakovica forward command post of the Pristina Corps, in fact, sir, when you said that that was not true, that is not correct, is it? He may have -- Mr. Peraj could be completely correct when he is saying that, that General Lazarevic was commanding this action?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the same thing to go and inspect a unit and to go and command a unit. That action in Meja started in the morning on the 27th, and I was with General Lazarevic around 11.00, 12.00. There was a cocktail afterwards, a reception, and we stayed, say, until 2.00 or 3.00. For him to go and command, he would have to go to the command post first, familiarise himself with the situation, and then command. However, that is not what happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But you really don't know, sir, if that's what happened because you've told us that you do not know what were the whereabouts of General Lazarevic once you left that awards ceremony?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've also told us today earlier in your evidence that when you were speaking about General Lazarevic, that he was someone who would tour units in the field and who would always be informed of actions that would take place that involved his units, correct? You recall saying that when you were speaking about him?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no dispute in terms of that. He had units all over Kosovo and Metohija. It's action Reka, but he had actions going on throughout Kosovo and Metohija and he could have gone to inspect any unit at any point in time. I really don't know where General Lazarevic was when I left Pristina. I don't know, and it wasn't his obligation to tell me, and it's not customary for me to ask him where he went.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So he could have gone to the forward command post of -- in Djakovica of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm saying that I did not see him. I was not there either. I was not at the command post, that is. I did not see him, and I know that he stayed on after me. That's what I can tell you. I cannot speculate as to where he was, whether he could have arrived there, whether he did arrive there and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So the truth is, you don't know? You don't know if he was there or not?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The truth is that I did not see him there and that he stayed on in Pristina after I left.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say "I did not see him there," did you personally go to the forward command post of the Pristina Corps while this action was taking place?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you wouldn't know if he was there or not? You weren't there?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not there. My Chief of Staff, Colonel Stankovic, was there, and he would have told me had the commander come. If the commander was in Djakovica, I'd have to know that. Whenever the commander came, I as brigade commander was duty-bound to meet him there, to salute him, report to him, and if the corps commander came to Djakovica, I would have to know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: But, sir, based on what you've told us about General Lazarevic as a commander and the way he kept himself well informed of the actions of his units, you would agree with me that an action of this nature involving so many different units of the Pristina Corps Command would be an action that he would have been fully informed of?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it's not that that many units participated. If it was the case, it was parts of units. You showed me the 125th Brigade document a few moments ago, I believe what I saw in the commander's report. He said part of his unit, and then part of my unit was there. Now, if someone were to interpret this, they might say two brigades. However, that didn't even have to be two companies, to say it could have been two companies only. That is not any kind of meaningful force that it would be a task of primary importance for the corps commander. The corps commander deals with other matters. After all, it is not customary for the chief of the staff of the corps to be at the same place where the corps commander is. The Chief of Staff of the corps was certainly there. Colonel Milan Kotur was the one who was in charge of the action, so I assert that General Lazarevic was not there, to the best of my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, but you don't know that for sure?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot be sure because I wasn't with him all the time, stuck to him. How could I know? Also, I would have been informed had he come to Djakovica, but my Chief of Staff did not inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've told us that. Sir, when actions were carried out by Pristina Corps units that involved multiple units, would these actions have to have the approval of the Pristina Corps Commander before being carried out?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A forward command post had the right to make decisions. Therefore, I don't know about that. I do know that the tasks that I received from the forward command post I treated the same way as any other task that I was given by the corps commander. I cannot go into that now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, could a large-scale action involving multiple units of the Pristina Corps be launched without the knowledge of General Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You don't know. You don't know whether he had to approve actions that involved multiple units of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The forward command post was in Djakovica, and the Chief of Staff was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you about General Lazarevic, not about the Pristina -- the Djakovica forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he had to know or not. I cannot give you an answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You don't know whether he had to be even informed of actions that involved multiple units of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: To approve is one thing and to be informed is another. I'm sure that he could have been informed.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you are saying that large-scale operations that involve multiple units did not require his approval? They did not require the approval of the commander of the Pristina Corps; is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Your answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, units did not participate. It was parts of units that participated. If parts of units participate, depending on the size of the force involved, he may or may not be informed. However, the forward command post in Djakovica had the right to plan and order us commanders to carry out certain actions that had been planned according to their concept. I cannot go into the relationships and authority between the forward command post and the corps. I cannot tell you exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm not asking that, sir. You said that depending on the size of the force involved, he may or not be informed. So I take it from that, sir, that you were speaking about a sizeable operation involving multiple units or sections of units, however you want to call it? This is something that he would have been informed about?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is something that he would have had to approve before the operation or the action was launched, if we are talking about a large-scale sizeable action involving multiple units?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. What I do know is that I had to receive from the corps commander everything that had to do with my unit, or I can receive a task from the forward command post. You are asking me to go into some kind of relationships that go beyond my powers. The corps command is above my level. I know what my obligations are vis-à-vis the corps command, and I know what the rights of the corps command are in respect of me. As for the relations between the forward command post and the corps command and corps commander, I don't know about that in great detail, and the situation may vary from one case to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay, sir, we'll leave that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The objection is no longer valid because the question has been answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I want to - we have very little time left today - show you another statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is, in fact, I should point out, Your Honours, in the English it's part of D730, but we noticed when looking at this document that the corresponding B/C/S translation hasn't been uploaded as part of D730, so we have uploaded it as a separate exhibit in e-court for the purpose of being able to show the witness the B/C/S version of the document. And this is 65 ter 60 -- 06050. If we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is, again, a statement that you prepared for the Commission of Co-operation, and it's dated also 27th of December, 2002, like the one we had looked at previously, and it refers to activities of your unit on the 28th of April, 1999. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, when you -- this statement -- when you prepared this statement and the previous one that we looked at, did you consult any other documents other than the book or report "As Seen, As Told?"

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we had no documents. We had no documents made available to us. It was only based on memory and memory only.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've told us, sir, that you yourself didn't participate in the Reka action, correct? You weren't involved, it was your subordinate, Mr. Zlatko Odak?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was not there. I just visited them. I checked on that unit, but I was not involved in the action itself, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if I understood your evidence yesterday and today correctly, the information that you have about this operation is the information that Mr. Odak gave to you?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So just drawing your attention, sir, to paragraph 2. We see at the bottom part you are referring to a seal-off operation on the following line, and then you said: "To the left trig point 442, to the right 478 Batraki, aimed at preventing the withdrawal of STS on the axis Racaj village - Skivljan village." You see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you say at the bottom of the statement: "I hereby state categorically that neither I nor anyone else from my unit committed or participated in any war crime during that time. I also do not have any knowledge that such a crime was perpetrated by any other unit." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I take it you stand by that, what you stated here?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this exhibit into evidence 65 ter 0650.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P01539.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if your subordinate Major Odak was interviewed by this commission in relation to this incident that we've been discussing?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that he did testify here.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm asking if he gave a statement to this same Commission for Co-operation with the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, this commission, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And were you present during the time that he gave his statement?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Did you consult his statement before preparing yours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you had a look at his statement before you did yours?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I had asked you earlier, sir, if you had consulted any other sources other than the book called "As Seen, As Told," and you had told me that you had not. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not any document, but I didn't mean statements. I mean, I thought documents that could be found in archives and things like that. I'm saying that I did not look at other documents from the brigade from that given period, but Odak's statement, yes, I did have a look at that. If you meant at that point in time when you were asking me whether I looked at something like his statement too, then I certainly did. I'm saying now, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if we could have that up on the screen, it's 65 ter 06045.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just going to draw your attention to the bottom of this document if we could scroll it down, the paragraph beginning with, "On the 25th of April, I was given the task," and I'd like to direct your attention to the sentence that refers to the following line for the seal-off operation and then it indicates the trig point for the operation, and it goes on to say, "with the aim of preventing the withdrawal of STS on the axis Racaj village -- Skivljan village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The aim of his unit I carried out indispensable preparations for carrying out combat task within which I regulated; is that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The procedure for the unit and individuals in the event of encountering the Siptar terrorist forces --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, sir, I'm going to stop you there because we are running out of time. Sir, I put to you that this sentence that refers to the trig point and the aim of preventing the action is, in fact, almost verbatim in this statement that you prepared for the commission?

utterances.speaker: MILOS DOSAN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did say that I used Odak's statement because I wasn't there. I wrote my statement on the basis of his statement. Just as the commission gave me the task of writing my statement, I called him and I said, "How did all of that go, write it up." Because he was there all the time. I was there for 10 or 15 minutes. I went there, I visited them, made certain remarks, and left. As for the events that are being asked about here, my only knowledge comes from him as commander of the unit. I never said that I was there all the time. My statement is based on Major Odak's statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So you looked at the statement and made sure that both statements contained the same information?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think the answer of the witness was that he had asked the major to write what occurred. He then read what the major wrote and he wrote his statement based on what the major had said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I withdraw that question. Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We do need to stop.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I seek to tender this exhibit and my apologies for going over time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P01540.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know what the possibilities of the Court are, but our request, the request of the Defence is to go on for about 10 minutes or so. The redirect will be very short so if Ms. Kravetz does not have many more questions, then we would complete our redirect very quickly, and we would greatly appreciate it if you could extend our working hours a bit so that we would finish this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We would often like to accommodate you, Mr. Popovic, but that sort of request creates many problems. They are problems about transport and your client being returned to custody. There are problems about the times for the interpreters and the other support staff, some of whom are outside this courtroom, and my experience is that those problems are such that it is not justified for us to extend our time. I'm sorry about that, but given the time that's been spent with the witness in examination-in-chief, I don't think we can hurry Ms. Kravetz, and I don't believe that in fairness to the administrative organisation, that we can just on the spur of the moment extend the hearing. So we must continue tomorrow. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 17th day of February, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.
